description:
Advances: specled.package, specled.triangulation

Go-live gate ticket (2026-07-25): the shipped .spec/ corpus is the adoption-facing proof of the spec-code-test integrity pitch and must contain no provably false statements at launch. Split out of specled_-vk0, which keeps only the deferred hardening work (lookbehind bounds, severity-corpus asymmetry, digit codes, stale-marker sweep, two-way mirror).

Two live inaccuracies, both verified against code during the 2026-07-24 triage (see specled_-vk0 description + last comment for full evidence):

1. package.spec.md doc_identifier_integrity must OVERCLAIMS: the lint guards 3 of at least 5 emitted finding-code namespaces — evidence/* (emitted at lib/specled_ex/evidence/store.ex:46, evidence/sync.ex:266,431,455, mix/tasks/spec.prune.ex:47-60, spec.sync.ex:41), detector_unavailable (lib/specled_ex/review.ex:537), and spec_requirement_too_short are unguarded; the corpus merely happens to be clean today. Fix: widen @token_patterns to cover the unguarded namespaces OR narrow the must to claim only what is guarded. Maintainer call on widen-vs-narrow, then mechanical.

2. triangulation.spec.md scenario asserts a given/when the implementation and tests do not perform (fabricated scenario text found in the specled_-6fn ship-it critical review, restated in the specled_-vk0 comment). Fix: rewrite the scenario to describe actual behavior, through append-only ceremony.

NOT in scope here (already covered by specled_-dn4.8, which is being finished as part of the P1 dn4 epic): F37 boundary_row_preferred_on_flush contradicting a must in the same file, and F39 coverage qualifier ids asserting the opposite of their names. Do not double-fix.

Verification: mix spec.check green + the corpus-scoped doc-identifier lint; per-claim code citations above make each fix mechanically checkable.

MAINTAINER CALL (widen-vs-narrow): both. Widening alone still left the must claiming more
than the lint holds; narrowing alone would have left two real namespaces unguarded.

Scope note for the auditor — two deviations from the ticket text, both in the honest
direction:

     8-code family, already referenced in the corpus. Without it, the must's new
     enumeration would itself have been false — the exact defect class this ticket exists
     to remove.
  2. The ticket's cited unguarded set (evidence/*, detector_unavailable,
     spec_requirement_too_short) is incomplete: verifier.ex and tag_findings.ex emit
     several dozen more bare codes. The must therefore characterizes the unguarded set
     rather than enumerating it, since any enumeration would rot.

Deliberately NOT done (ADR-constrained): specled.decision.doc_identifier_lint_spec_corpus
explicitly rejects reflection over lib/ to derive the code set, so no lib-scanning
completeness test was added. A new namespace landing in future is therefore still
unguarded until someone adds it by hand — that is the accepted trade, and the ADR now
records the family list it applies to. The two-way mirror and stale-marker sweep remain
with specled_-vk0 as scoped.

Summary: Widened the doc-identifier lint from three to five guarded finding-code families
(adding evidence/* and cross_field/*, 15 codes) and rewrote the doc_identifier_integrity
must to state the boundary it actually enforces — shape-detectable namespaces are
mechanically guarded, bare snake_case codes stay author-enforced because their stems
collide with legitimate non-code identifiers in the scanned corpus. Rewrote the
triangulation test_only_change_scenario_gate scenario's given/when to describe the
CoverageTriangulation.findings/3 call the covering test actually makes, replacing a

Semantic checks:
- Spec stubs run: 2, passed: 2 — package.spec.md tagged_tests (execute: true, covers doc_identifier_integrity) and triangulation.spec.md tagged_tests (execute: true, covers pure_function). No stubs were flipped by this commit; both were already execute: true.

Would fail if any evidence/* or cross_field/* token in the corpus were misspelled or removed from lib — the unknown-token assertion reports the offending file and token. The new test at :238 additionally would fail if a family were added to @known_codes but not @token_patterns (fake token returns [] instead of [fake]) or to @token_patterns but not @known_codes (real token returns [real] instead of []). Would fail if findings/3 began consulting Mix globals or reading a coverage artifact from disk and the two calls diverged (assert first == second), or if it began emitting drift/untested findings from ambient state (the non-detector_unavailable code list would be non-empty). The scenario's own then-clauses are covered at :52 — refute on branch_guard_untested_realization scoped to subject_id, and refute on branch_guard_realization_drift with no subject scope, matching the rewritten "not emitted at all". Seams: none — real CoverageTriangulation.findings/3 against literal input maps.
- Intent-level scope concerns: none. No change touches F37 boundary_row_preferred_on_flush or the F39 coverage qualifier ids; no spec was weakened to make code pass (the must was made narrower AND the lint wider, so the guarded set strictly grew from 3 families to 5).
- Targeted verification: pass. mix compile --warnings-as-errors clean; mix test on both touched files (10 tests, 0 failures); mix test --only spec:specled.package.doc_identifier_integrity (0 failures); mix test --only spec:specled.triangulation.pure_function (0 failures); mix spec.check --no-run-commands → validate status=pass errors=0 warnings=0, branch findings=0, spec.check result=pass; mix format --check-formatted clean; mix deps.unlock --check-unused clean. No stubs flipped, so none to re-run.
- Corpus-scoped claims (per step 7.5): 11 validated, 11 by execution. No falsehoods found.
  1. "Exactly five emitted families are shape-detectable" — TRUE, verified exhaustively rather than by reading. Sweeping lib/ for every slash-namespaced string literal yields only append_only/*, overlap/*, evidence/*, cross_field/* plus four non-codes (refs/heads, refs/remotes, origin/main, n/a). The only prefix family is branch_guard_*. No slash-namespaced literals exist in priv/. Sweeping the scanned corpus for a sixth backticked namespace family returns only `actions/cache` and `actions/checkout` (GitHub Actions), which match no token pattern. No dynamic code construction ("ns/" <> x) exists anywhere in lib.

  3. @cross_field_codes 8/8 emitted, all in lib/specled_ex/decision_parser/cross_field.ex: supersedes_missing_replaces:84, supersedes_unresolved_replaces:93, reverses_what_missing:117, affects_empty:136, affects_unresolved:163, missing_change_type:182, adr_field_drift:222, adr_status_regression:242.
  4. Reverse direction also clean, which matters because a lib code missing from @known_codes would flag correct prose as fabricated: lib emits exactly the 10 append_only/*, 2 overlap/*, and 10 branch_guard_* codes the lists name — set equality, not just containment, on all five families.
  5. "detector_unavailable" is emitted — lib/specled_ex/coverage_triangulation.ex:101 and :1043.
  6. "spec_requirement_too_short" is emitted — @finding_code at lib/specled_ex/config/prose.ex:98.
  7. The must's collision example "detector_unavailable_by_leg is a review-output field" — real, lib/specled_ex/review.ex:508,524,535.
  8. Its second example, requirement ids sharing the stem — real, specled.triangulation.detector_unavailable_on_missing_coverage at .spec/specs/triangulation.spec.md:109. So the claim that a detector_[a-z_]+ pattern would reject correct prose is demonstrable, not hand-waved.
  9. "mix spec.check never runs triangulation" — TRUE, verified three ways. lib/mix/tasks/spec.check.ex contains zero references to triangulation, CoverageTriangulation, or SpecLedEx.Review, and makes no Mix.Task.run delegation. The only CoverageTriangulation consumers in lib/ are lib/mix/tasks/spec.triangle.ex and lib/specled_ex/review/coverage_closure.ex, the latter reached only from lib/specled_ex/review.ex:63 via lib/mix/tasks/spec.review.ex:55. And no spec-verification `kind: command` target invokes spec.triangle or spec.review — the single package.spec.md command mentioning spec.review only calls Mix.Task.get (loads, does not run).
  10. Provenance claim "(Decision 1, specled.decision.aggregate_first_spec_coverage)" — verified at both ends per step 10. The definition exists: maintainer decision 1 at .spec/decisions/specled.decision.aggregate_first_spec_coverage.md:58-60, "Triangulation consumers are mix spec.triangle and mix spec.review only. mix spec.check does not run triangulation and never will." The ADR restates and relies on it at :184-186 ("per maintainer decision 1") and :294. The scenario's use matches the definition; no contradiction.
  11. ADR file-path claim ".../config/branch_guard_test.exs" resolves — test/specled_ex/config/branch_guard_test.exs exists, so the lookbehind rationale cites a real file.
- Full-suite verification: not run by verifier (by design)
- Audit-expanded scope (per step 11): none — no prior AUDIT: BOUNCE comment on this ticket.

Verdict: PASS

Both provably false statements named by the ticket are gone, and the replacements are true. The must no longer claims mechanical coverage the lint lacks, and it enumerates the guarded families correctly including cross_field/*, which the ticket text omitted — the implementer's deviation 1 was necessary, not scope creep: without it the new enumeration would itself have been false. The rewritten scenario's when/then now match test/integration/scenario_test_only_change_test.exs line for line, and the fabricated mix spec.cover.test + mix spec.check flow is replaced by a claim I confirmed independently against lib/.

Gaps: none.

Notes (advisory, none change the verdict):
- The rewritten scenario's third given, "a branch that edits only the covering test file, leaving the closure unchanged", is still narrative — the test creates no branch and edits no file; it models the precondition by holding closure_map and coverage records fixed. This is unchanged in kind from the pre-commit given ("a branch that edits only the test (no code change)"), which the ticket did not identify as the falsehood, and the test's own header comment (:12-25) states the same premise, so spec and test agree. The falsehood the ticket targeted was the fabricated command flow in given 2 / when, and that is fixed. Advisory only.
- pure_function's "shall not touch the filesystem, start processes, or consult Mix globals" is proven by idempotence plus input-only arguments, not by actually trapping filesystem or process access. A findings/3 that read a file deterministically would still pass. Pre-existing, not introduced by this commit; worth a hardening ticket if the purity claim needs to be load-bearing.
- The ADR edit leaves three awkward mid-sentence line wraps ("Its corpus\nwas the user-facing…", "Every\nother emitted code is a\nbare snake_case identifier"). Cosmetic; markdown is not format-checked. Worth a one-line rewrap if this file gets touched again.
- The widened evidence/* pattern is now shape-sensitive to prose: an unbackticked path fragment written as "evidence/store.ex" at a line start (not preceded by / or a word char) would be flagged as a fabricated code. The corpus is clean today, so this is latent, not live. It belongs with the specled_-vk0 lookbehind-bounds work already scoped there.
- Reporting honestly: `agent-session lines` in this cold-verify subagent returns the same session id the implementer reported, because agent-session resolves the harness session rather than the subagent. The verification itself was performed cold — ticket, specs, ADR, and diff were read fresh, and every code claim was re-derived from lib/ rather than taken from the implementer's comment.
